title: STP/BPDU Violation — CONF-A-TV01
summary: An unmanaged switch with spanning tree enabled is inserted between the conference display and its access port. The first BPDU triggers BPDU Guard, which err-disables the port. SentinelSwitch confirms the err-disable from syslog, attributes the port to the last known endpoint, applies an administrative hold so errdisable auto-recovery cannot re-enable the port, and records the evidence.
mechanism: BPDU Guard err-disable (switch-native) + SentinelSwitch administrative hold
resolution_note: Unmanaged switch removed from conference room; display reconnected directly. Port recovered with shutdown / no shutdown.

title: Unauthorized Endpoint — unknown device DC:A6:32:19:77:C1
summary: A single-board computer that is not in the asset inventory is connected to a spare corporate drop. MAC Authentication Bypass is rejected by FreeRADIUS, no 802.1X supplicant responds, and SentinelSwitch attributes the MAC to the physical interface using the AAA and syslog telemetry (the MAC address table has no entry because the port never became authorized).
resolution_note: Unregistered contractor single-board computer removed after physical inspection (ticket SVC-2026-0311). Port restored to service.

title: Rogue DHCP — VENDOR-LT-01
summary: A vendor laptop on the guest VLAN enables internet connection sharing, which starts a DHCP server on its wired interface. When the conference display is power-cycled and broadcasts DHCPDISCOVER, the laptop answers. DHCP snooping drops every OFFER and NAK arriving on the untrusted port and logs each drop; Suricata sees the offers on the SPAN feed and raises a local rule. SentinelSwitch attributes the server MAC to the port and shuts it down.
resolution_note: Vendor disabled connection sharing and left site. Port restored to service.
